graphite.hue: OKLCH hue 227 to 237, chroma at most 0.016
graphite.use: Dark surfaces, a cool graphite with a faint teal-blue undertone under the brand teal. graphite1 page, graphite2 raised, graphite3 sunk and hover, graphite4 overlay, graphite5 hairline, graphite6 strong line, graphite7 control border (3:1 on graphite1 through graphite4).

ink.use: Text on dark, a cool near-white and cool greys. ink1 primary, ink2 soft, ink3 muted, ink4 faint: decoration, disabled labels and code comments (4.5:1 on graphite1 through graphite3).

green.use: Brand, a teal-green, and the colour of Pan in the wordmark, the mark and the terminal rails. green400 is the focal green on graphite. green300 hover, green500 pressed, green700 text and links on light, green950 and green50 washes. Never a state colour.

azure.use: Secondary, and the colour of Code in the wordmark. azure400 on dark, azure600 on light, azure950 and azure50 washes. Section numbers, version tags, one highlight per view. azure300 and azure700 also carry info. Never a fill behind body text, never an error or warning.

state.use: leaf is success, a true green at OKLCH hue 144, amber is warning, red is error, info takes azure, violet is data only. 300 is the foreground on dark, 700 on light, 950 and 50 are the washes. Success sits 26 degrees of hue from the brand teal so it never reads as the brand; every state also carries a glyph or a word.

mark.use: teal and orange exist for the mark and for art built from it, never for interface roles. teal400 is the midpoint of green400 and azure400; orange400 with amber300 is the warm point of the mark. The 700 steps are their light-ground forms.

cream.hue: OKLCH hue 86 to 88, chroma at most 0.02
cream.use: Light surfaces, a warm cream. cream1 raised and overlay, cream2 page, cream3 sunk and hover, cream4 hairline, cream5 strong line, cream6 control border (3:1 on cream1 through cream3).

slate.hue: OKLCH hue 226 to 237, chroma at most 0.015
slate.use: Text on light, a dark graphite. slate1 primary, slate2 soft, slate3 muted, slate4 faint: decoration and disabled labels.

code.note: Code blocks and terminal frames take the theme: graphite slabs on dark, cream wells with dark graphite ink on light. Product captures and recordings keep the ground they were recorded on.

terminal.note: Nearest fixed-palette projections of the roles, for surfaces without truecolor. At 16 colours the brand teal is cyan and success is green, so the two stay apart.

display.use: Headings and the wordmark. Weight 700, tight tracking.

text.use: Body, navigation and controls. Weights 400, 500 and 600.

mono.use: Commands, code, labels, section numbers and data. Weights 400 and 500.

radius.use: xs inline code and tags, sm buttons and inputs, md panels, code blocks, cards and menus, lg hero media and dialogs, pill status chips and switches only. A nested element takes the outer radius minus the gap.

border.use: Hairlines separate, control borders mark things that take input, emphasis marks the one selected or primary thing. The focus ring is always offset so the ground shows between the control and the ring.

elevation.note: On dark, height is a lighter graphite step plus a hairline; a shadow appears only on overlays, where it darkens content underneath. On light, height is the lighter cream1 on the cream2 page plus a soft shadow.

surfaces.2: paper-sunk with a line-strong border: menus, popovers, sticky bars
surfaces.3: paper-overlay with a line-strong border: dialogs

dark.brand: 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 60%, transparent), 0 0 28px color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 32%, transparent)
dark.accent: 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in srgb, var(--secondary) 60%, transparent), 0 0 28px color-mix(in srgb, var(--secondary) 30%, transparent)
dark.halo: radial-gradient(closest-side, color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 22%, transparent), transparent)

allowed: the mark and wordmark where they are the subject of the view (hero, welcome, app splash)
the one primary action on hover and keyboard focus
one hero media frame per page
a live indicator: a running cursor, an active worker dot
never: body text, headings in running content, or links
panels, cards, tables, inputs or code blocks at rest
the light theme, where every glow token resolves to none
more than one glowing element in view at a time

naming: PanCode is the product in prose, headings and metadata; pancode is the command, package, binary and paths, always in the mono face.
The interfaces are PanCode in the terminal and PanCode on the desktop. No separate product names, marks or mascots.
The wordmark is set PanCode in one word with a capital P and C: Pan in the brand green, Code in the secondary azure. In block letters it stacks PAN over CODE.
rules: Say what the reader can do, with the command that does it.
Short declarative sentences, present tense, second person. No exclamation marks.
Name real things: the file, the flag, the model, the limit.
State limits and alpha status where the reader chooses the feature.
Interface labels are verbs or nouns in sentence case; errors say what happened and what to do next.
Never use a dash to interrupt a sentence with a clause; write a second sentence.
